text:
incident-bot: p95/p99 spike detected on inference-path — streaming stalls increasing since 03:14 UTC, currently p99 1.8s above baseline and several customer streams stuck in 'waiting for tokens'. Auto-alerting oncall.

Maya Nguyen: seeing it in the dashboards too, spike corresponds with repeated 503s from config-fetch service and auth rate-limit bursts.

Sam Ortiz: confirmed, control-plane config fetch latency jumped 10x around 03:13. Many streaming requests blocked waiting on feature flag check.

Lee Carter: digging logs now, looks like featureflag-service has a cache miss storm for rollout v3 (new staging rollout). Lots of DB RPS around feature_flags table.

Carla R.: @Maya @Sam any sign of deployments or infra changes around that time? I don't see scheduled deploys in the window.

Maya Nguyen: nothing in eng-releases. We did have a small rollout of a flags change at 03:10 by an automation job — might be related.

Sam Ortiz: reproducing locally: when featureflag times out, inference path pauses awaiting flags -> streaming stalls. We need a fallback quickly to avoid more customer impact.

oncall-bot: paging Lee Carter (oncall), escalation to SRE lead if not acknowledged in 2m.

Lee Carter: ack. I'm going to rate-limit the config-fetch calls from controlplane to 100qps and flip fallback to cached-flags for 5m. Doing it now.

Kevin B.: heads-up: cached-flags fallback will allow stale flags for a short window, documented risk is minor compared to ongoing stalls. Agree.

Sam Ortiz: patching fallback now — command I'm running:

```bash
# enable cached flags fallback
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/flags/fallback -d '{"mode":"cached","ttl_s":300}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $CI_TOKEN"
```

Carla R.: putting a mitigation note on status page draft: "Reduced latency by enabling cached flag fallback; customers may see delayed flag updates for ~5 minutes" — anyone object?

Maya Nguyen: good. Also let's increase auth token rate limits for controlplane->auth to absorb burst. Hitting auth 429s too.

Lee Carter: raised temporary quota on auth-service for controlplane API key id cp-main for 10 minutes. Request backlog is draining.

Sam Ortiz: watching metric — p99 dropped from a 2.4s spike to ~400ms within 45s of fallback+quota bump. Streaming success percent recovering.

incident-bot: incident severity upgraded to Sev2 due to SLO impact on streaming tail latency > 3% of traffic in last 10m.

Maya Nguyen: can we identify customers impacted? Querying request logs for streaming stall traces.

Sam Ortiz: quick query shows ~1.8k streaming sessions affected in the last 15m, top tenants: tenant-neo (~520 sessions), partner-x (~220), internal-load-test (~150).

Carla R.: starting outreach to top tenants. I'll spin up messages for support and CSMs.

Kevin B.: note about root cause: featureflag-service had a cache eviction bug combined with a runaway rollout job that caused DB hot rows. We should rollback or pause that rollout.

Lee Carter: pausing rollout v3 now. Patch to the rollout scheduler in prod to stop incremental updates.

Sam Ortiz: after rollback + cached fallback + auth quota bump, token auth 429s dropped to baseline, config-fetch latency back to normal. Re-checking traces for residual stalls.

Maya Nguyen: streaming tail p99 still slightly elevated but trending down. Recommend keeping cached-fallback for 5 more minutes then revert once no regressions.

Carla R.: outreach message draft: "We observed elevated streaming latency due to control-plane feature flag service overload. Mitigations applied — cached fallbacks + temporary auth quota bump + rollout paused. If you saw stream stalls, please file a support ticket and include trace ids. We're monitoring. Apologies for the disruption."

incident-bot: creating incident ticket INC-2026-1904567890 and attaching key metrics snapshot.

Lee Carter: adding a short-term fix in runtime: skip realtime feature-flag RPC for streaming requests and rely on last-known flags when under controlplane error. I'll drop a PR to eng-runtime for review.

Sam Ortiz: collecting logs/traces for postmortem. Capturing the timeline and the rollout job id.

Maya Nguyen: oncall handoff in 20m — Sam, can you own the overnight watch and postmortem notes? I'll take notes for status and coordinate with support for customer comms.

Sam Ortiz: yep — I'll own the follow-up, postmortem, and make a recommendation for hardened cache behavior + rollout rate-limits.

Carla R.: support pinged the top tenants and we've got a response from tenant-neo noting a 50% failure rate on streaming connections—they want a postmortem. We'll escalate to account team.

Kevin B.: action items assigned:
- Lee: PR to runtime to provide local fallback for flags (urgent)
- Sam: compile traces, create postmortem draft
- Maya: coordinate customer comms, update status page
- Carla: notify account teams for top impacted tenants
- Infra: add guardrails to rollout scheduler (rate-limit + circuit-breaker)

Maya Nguyen: last check before handoff — p99 now within SLO threshold, streaming success ~98.7% in last 5m. I'll hand to Sam in 15.

oncall-bot: handoff reminder sent to Sam Ortiz (next oncall) at 03:55 UTC.

Sam Ortiz: ack, I'll watch for regressions and pull the postmortem together.

Maya Nguyen: thanks everyone — nice rapid mitigation. We'll follow up with a full postmortem and timeline later today. :thumbsup:
